page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c6a.large is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture with 2 dedicated vCPUs and 2 physical cores, utilizing the AMD EPYC 7H12 processor running at a base clock speed of 2.6 GHz. The CPU configuration includes a 32 KB L1 data cache, 0.5 MB L2 cache, and 16 MB L3 cache. The instance is equipped with 4.0 GB of system memory, yielding a resource density of 2.0 GB of RAM per core. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, and relies on a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks indicate that the ecs.c6a.large sits primarily in the lower tiers for heavy computational workloads. Stress-ng single-core and multi-core CPU tests, along with PassMark CPU and physics tests, place the instance in the bottom 10% of performance. Similarly, memory bandwidth tests show poor read-only performance at 99.87 GB/sec for cached small blocks and 22.35 GB/sec for uncached large blocks, while write bandwidth is weak at 14.76 GB/sec. However, the instance demonstrates average performance in single-threaded tasks, such as gzip compression (24.5 GB/sec), bzip3 decompression (9.16 GB/sec), and Geekbench single-core execution (score of 1281.0). Multi-core execution, software compilation, and database operations remain in the bottom 10%.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the ecs.c6a.large offers a low-cost entry point for dedicated AMD EPYC resources, trading off high-end multi-core throughput and memory bandwidth for predictable, non-shared CPU allocation. Given its performance profile, this instance is best suited for lightweight, single-threaded tasks, basic web serving, simple utility scripting, or development environments that do not require high memory capacity, local storage, or intensive parallel processing.
